title: Driving Rules in Albania: Who Goes First at Roundabouts Guide
excerpt: Learn the essential driving rules in Albania, from roundabout etiquette to strict safety laws, so you can enjoy a smooth summer road trip without fines.
intro: When you pick up your car from AutoConnect Rental at Tirana Airport, the first thing you’ll notice is the steady flow of traffic on the right‑hand side. Albania’s roads are beautiful but demand respect for local rules, especially at the many roundabouts that dot the highway network. This guide breaks down the most important driving rules in Albania so you can navigate confidently and avoid costly mistakes.

sections.title: Driving Rules in Albania: Roundabout Basics
sections.body: Albanian roundabouts are common on the A1 highway and in city centres such as Tirana and Durrës. They are usually marked with a white circular island and a yield sign at the entry. Vehicles travel clockwise on the right‑hand side, and you must give way to traffic already circulating. Enter only when there is a clear gap, and keep a steady speed to merge smoothly. Pedestrians may cross at designated crosswalks on the outer edge, but they are rare on major roundabouts. Understanding this layout is the first step to navigating the country safely.

sections.title: Right‑of‑Way at Albanian Roundabouts
sections.body: Right‑of‑way at Albanian roundabouts follows a simple principle: traffic already inside the circle has priority. When you approach, look to your left and yield to any vehicle that is moving around the island. If two cars arrive simultaneously, the one on the left proceeds first. This rule is part of the broader driving rules in Albania and applies to both cars and motorcycles. Keep your turn signals on when you intend to leave the roundabout, and watch for cyclists who may use the inner lane. Respecting this order reduces the risk of sudden braking and collisions.

sections.title: Key Safety Rules for Summer Drivers
sections.body: Summer visitors often overlook a few non‑negotiable safety rules. Headlights must stay on 24 hours a day, even on clear nights, so keep them switched on as soon as you leave the airport. Seatbelts are compulsory for every passenger, front and rear. The legal blood‑alcohol limit is 0.01 %, effectively a zero‑tolerance policy—any amount can lead to a fine or arrest. Mobile phone use is banned unless you have a certified hands‑free system, with penalties up to €100. Speed limits are 40 km/h in built‑up areas and 80 km/h on rural roads; always adjust to local conditions.

sections.title: Avoiding Common Fines and What to Do in an Emergency
sections.body: Fines in Albania can add up quickly if you ignore the rules. Using a handheld phone while driving costs between €25 and €100, and driving without a seatbelt incurs a similar penalty. If you are stopped for exceeding the speed limit, the fine is calculated per kilometre over the limit. In case of an accident, call the police at 129 and stay at the scene. Exchange contact details with the other driver and take photos of the damage. Most rental agencies, including AutoConnect Rental, will assist you with the paperwork, but having your insurance documents ready speeds up the process.

tip.title: Pro Tip: Keep Headlights On From the Moment You Pick Up Your Car
tip.body: Albanian police routinely check that headlights are on, even during daylight. Turning them on as soon as you collect your vehicle at Tirana Airport prevents an instant fine and makes you more visible on the winding coastal roads.

faq.question: Who has the right of way in an Albanian roundabout?
faq.answer: Traffic already circulating inside the roundabout has priority. Vehicles entering must yield to those already moving clockwise around the island. If two cars arrive at the same time, the one on the left proceeds first.

faq.question: What is the alcohol limit for driving in Albania?
faq.answer: Albania enforces a 0.01 % blood‑alcohol limit, effectively a zero‑tolerance policy. Any detectable alcohol can result in a fine, license suspension, or arrest.

faq.question: Do I need an international driving permit for Albania?
faq.answer: A valid EU driving licence is accepted throughout Albania. Visitors from non‑EU countries should carry an International Driving Permit (IDP) together with their home‑country licence.
